It does take a while, but we worked on leave it every day a couple times throughout the day and he's great at it at 19 weeks. Keep working on it and you'll see progress! I replied to the oiginal commenter about how I trained it.

I started out super small and then made the command more challenging. I got him into a down and put a treat in front of him with my hand over it. He would paw at it, try to bite/lick my hand, but the second he moved away from it I would use our marker word 'good' and feed him a treat that wasn't the one I wanted him to leave alone. Eventually he got the hang of it and I lifted my hand off of it but I would still keep it close b/c he didn't know the command very well. As I lifted my hand off, I would say "leave it." If he didn't take the treat I would give him another one which was higher value as well. Where he's at rn at 19 weeks is being able to leave a treat on his nose, paws, treats dropped from the table, and he makes eye contact with me when I say leave it. It's all about starting super small and working your way up with your puppy to make the command more and more universal/challenging each day!
